children: was found guilty by a New Mexico jury of being liable for deceiving users about privacy protections on the platform. The decision was the second that went against the company in the state this year, although appeal processes could take years to play out.

The jury found over 43M violations of state consumer protection law, and it is now up to the judge to determine how much the company will pay, with attorneys representing the state asking for the maximum $5K penalty per violation.

"The verdict marks a significant victory for New Mexico consumers and holds one of the world’s largest technology companies accountable for its conduct," read a statement from the New Mexico Department of Justice.
New Mexico's attorney general sued the company in 2021, arguing that Meta
was selling that data to third-party apps while misleading users. The case drew widespread attention because it was tied to the controversial political consulting firm Cambridge Analytica.

title: Facebook loses high-profile case in New Mexico over deceiving users
